tested_scope: One self-contained deterministic local idempotency/retry fixture only, continuing the prior acknowledgement-loss unknown-outcome case for stable effect_identity=E. The pre-reconciliation canonical branch is intentionally two-valued because an acknowledgement-loss client cannot infer commit success: branch B0 has canonical_effect_count=0 (the original mutation did not commit) and branch B1 has canonical_effect_count=1 (the original mutation committed once). On the next invocation, fresh attempt_identity=A2 preserves stable effect_identity=E and must perform a canonical lookup before any mutation. This slice models that lookup itself being rate-limited or unavailable. The required policy is fail-closed: A2 emits no create/update in either branch, preserves outcome=unknown_pending_reconciliation, and checkpoints for a future invocation. Therefore the canonical count remains exactly 0 on B0 and exactly 1 on B1; the retry cannot increase the count while reconciliation evidence is unavailable. No real repository/API failure, simultaneous writer, public-source probe, O/downstream state, other-worker state, external hosted coordination, richer-mode execution, scheduler mutation, or optional second leaf was executed.
observations: When reconciliation lookup is unavailable, the deterministic policy submits no mutation in either possible canonical branch.

Because no mutation is submitted, canonical effect count cannot increase during this retry slice: it remains 0 if the original effect never committed and remains 1 if it committed once before acknowledgement loss.
Stable effect_identity=E and outcome=unknown_pending_reconciliation are preserved across the boundary so a later invocation can retry the read rather than replay the effect blindly.
The safety-preserving choice sacrifices immediate liveness: a persistent inability to perform the canonical lookup leaves the effect unresolved rather than risking a duplicate.
inference: Within this exact local fixture, fail-closed read-before-mutate reconciliation is sufficient to prevent a retry from increasing canonical effect cardinality when the reconciliation read itself is rate-limited or unavailable. This is a safety result only; it does not prove eventual progress, real API read consistency, simultaneous-writer safety, or that any particular repository surface exposes an authoritative lookup by stable effect identity.
